posts.text: Think I'm finally done here. Actually having fun on the sky app like it's 2019 again. See me there, same username 🫶👋

Trump has already established an EPA transition team led by two former fossil fuel lobbyists with “years of experience in dismantling environmental protections” 

I interviewed activists about where we go from here: heated.world/p/trumps-enviro…
My partner works for Wisp. Can confirm this is true. whnt.com/news/americans-stoc…
See, the Trump administration will protect access to clean air and water. Like it won't be widely available but definitely you will be able to access it somewhere

Trump’s re-election is the nail in the coffin for 1.5 degrees Celsius, the critical threshold past which the planet will experience significantly more extreme climate impacts, nine climate scientists and policy experts told us this week. heated.world/p/15c-is-dead-t…

I have a new answer to the question, “What does media need to do now that Trump has been re-elected?” I think you guys are really gonna like it


Rachel Donald (@CrisisReports)

WTF with @emorwee 

What a Trump Presidency means for climate action – with added humour because if you're not laughing you're crying amirite.

Listen to the full episode now: planetcritical.com/p/wtf-emi…

Video
  





— https://nitter.net/CrisisReports/status/1854642865172783524#m
Stepping outside on an 80 degree November day realizing not only that Donald Trump will be president for the next four years, but that this will be the coldest November for the rest of my life

America's oil execs have pocketed $1.4 billion selling stock during the Iran war, the WSJ reports

This cash windfall won’t go primarily toward yachts and private jets, but toward political campaigns and lobbying orgs dedicated to blocking climate policy and fueling authoritarianism

@emorwee.bsky.social: “What really makes this story remarkable is not simply that oil executives got rich from a war. It’s how perfectly legal and normal it all is, and what that legality reveals about who wins and who loses when America goes to war.” open.substack.com/pub/heated/p...

“When America goes to war, the costs are distributed broadly, onto every American who drives a car or heats a home. The benefits are distributed narrowly, flowing to a small group of men whose compensation is designed to capture exactly this kind of windfall.”

The top fear about EVs in my unscientific assessment (people reacting to the fact that I drive an EV) is, "Well, how do you charge it? Have you taken it on road trips?"

Yes, those require more planning. Yes, charging took a little while to figure out. But we're all smart people! We can do this!

New episode of the pod is out, debunking popular myths about electric vehicles and exploring research-based strategies to combat those myths

Particularly timely as gas prices drive up interest in EVs
Meanwhile, communities in Hawaii are paying for the true price of oil, digging their homes out from heavy volcanic mud after climate change-fueled extreme rain caused catastrophic flooding
Nothing like reliable, secure American energy!

Announcing a deal to pay $1 billion to stop two wind farms, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said: “The era of taxpayers subsidizing unreliable, unsecure energy is officially over.”

Hours later, a massive American oil refinery accidentally exploded, spiking gas prices nationwide

At an energy conference on Monday, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said, "The era of taxpayers subsidizing unreliable, unaffordable and unsecure energy is officially over.” 

Hours later, one of America’s largest oil refineries exploded.

I should add: Burgum was specifically applauding Trump’s deal to pay an offshore wind developer $1 billion to abandon its project and invest in oil and gas instead.

Ans the refinery explosion hours later sent gas prices soaring and forced nearby residents to shelter in place.

Just an extremely important piece from @emorwee.bsky.social in the Heated newsletter here. 

Oil prices have *ALWAYS* been fantastical and absurd, because it never factors in the shocking costs of what happens when you use it

Oil worker says fracking waste eroded his jaw. An elementary school was built atop the site where the radioactive waste was spread, journalist Saul Elbein reports.

How fossil fuel ads manipulate us. On today’s podcast, we watch and analyze fossil fuel ads.

Our reaction to the Steyer interview
Can a billionaire fix California?. Tom Steyer argues he's not a regular billionaire. He's a cool billionaire.
NBC's top climate reporter resigns. In an exclusive interview, veteran NBC meteorologist Chase Cain opens up about burnout, suppression, and why he's going independent.
Climate coverage is shrinking. We're expanding it.
Sam Alito has an oil money problem. Nearly 30 percent of Alito’s individual stock portfolio is directly tied to fossil fuels.

Trump is wiping out all climate regulation. Big Oil may regret it.  (by Julia Kane). For decades, oil majors fought climate regulation. Now, they’re afraid Trump’s extreme rollbacks could leave them on the hook to pay for what they’ve done.
Actually, I do know how to do this. In retrospect, paying attention to polluters may be one of the best ways to understand what’s currently happening in the United States.
